summary: The failing 'E2E Tests (Playwright)' check on PR #14 was never a Playwright failure. Its 'Build app' step ('npm run build' -> 'next build') hung because next.config.ts keeps eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds=false and typescript.ignoreBuildErrors=false, so the build runs a full-repo tsc inline; the 30m job cap killed it after 25m31s of silence and every E2E step was reported skipped. The underlying blocker is not QA-owned: on this same SHA the ci.yml 'Lint And Build' job measured Typecheck at 68m18s and failed with 1384 TypeScript errors across 189 files, because the generated Supabase types lack roughly 110 tables and 35 RPCs that product code queries. QA fixed the CI configuration and the two fail-open holes in the gate; the build cannot succeed until the type and migration-chain defects below are repaired.
completed: Proved from the run log that 'next build' printed 'Linting and checking validity of types ...' at 17:43:47Z and then produced no output for 25m31s before the job was cancelled by its 30m cap; steps 8-11 (Start app, Wait for app, Run E2E tests, upload artifact) were all 'skipped', so zero Playwright tests executed.

Established the cost split from the ci.yml 'Lint And Build' job on the identical SHA: Lint 48s, Typecheck 68m18s and failing. The webpack compile in the E2E job was only 3.0m, so the budget was consumed almost entirely by the inline typecheck.

Confirmed the proximate type failure with exact log evidence: lib/venue/staff-management.service.ts(148,35) TS2589, (149,13) TS2769, (155,5) TS2322, (162,14) TS2345, (168,7) TS2322, (184,7) TS2589, (184,21) TS2769, (185,7) TS2589, (185,21) TS2769.

Identified the root pattern: the argument-union errors name ~110 relations absent from the generated types, including venue_team_contractors, venue_crew_members, access_audit_log, user_profiles, projects, content, tracks, and about 35 RPCs including exec_sql, health_check and get_staff_dashboard_stats. Error volume is TS2339 495, TS2769 265, TS2322 180, TS2589 163, TS2345 161.

Traced the two headline venue tables to a single source: they are defined only in supabase/migrations/archive/enhanced_staff_management_schema.sql, which is not part of the active migration chain, and they are absent from types/database.types.ts (0 occurrences) and types/supabase.ts (0 occurrences).

Confirmed the same class of defect already tracked as DB-010 (archived worker-actions SQL marked local_only_unapplied) - this is a recurring archived-SQL-versus-active-chain reconciliation gap, not a one-off.

Captured the separate proximate failure of the 'Database Types' check on the same SHA: local Supabase replay aborts at 20260413200000_port_missing_tables.sql with 'ERROR: must be owner of table objects (SQLSTATE 42501)', so the generated-types comparison never runs.

ACTIONED IN PART, WITH ONE PART DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. (1) Root cause established with evidence: lib/database.types.ts is stale-forward AND the chain is short of the contract, so the defect is two-sided. The active chain creates 9 relations and 16 callables the generated types do not declare (watermark: the types reflect the chain through 20260910000001_get_active_organizer_account_for_org.sql), and 105 of the 107 object literals plus all 21 (table, column) pairs tsc rejects are absent from the chain entirely. (2) Every one of the 128 named objects is now classified with evidence in docs/engineering/database-type-inventory-2026-09-25.json (code-drift 107, schema-missing 9, unknown 10, stale-types 2) and routed to 23 handoffs naming the owning agent. (3) The SQLSTATE 42501 replay failure is fixed across all ten affected migrations and proved on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 instance: every original form aborts under a non-owner replay role, every guarded form completes with warnings, the owner-applied policy set is identical where the original worked, and five policies are recovered from a previously silent loss. (4) NOT DONE, deliberately: the three venue objects (venue_crew_members, venue_team_contractors, get_staff_dashboard_stats) were NOT re-created. The repository's own identity maps name organization_people and staff_members as the destinations, so re-creating them would resurrect a duplicate-risk surface. That decision is the venue domain's and is carried by HF-DB008-TYPECHECK-VENUE and HF-DB-008-VENUE-CREW-CONTRACTOR-SURFACE. (5) NOT DONE: `npm run typecheck` was not run. A full typecheck takes 68m18s on CI, OOMs on this 8GB box, and four lanes share it. The 50 diagnostics the database lane could prove are addressed by 20260925210000_venue_profile_presentation_columns.sql, and the rest is measured only after the clusters land.
next_steps: The typecheck blocker is NOT closed. It is decomposed: 2 objects are fixed by regenerating lib/database.types.ts against a reconciled target; 2 more (venue_profiles.social_links, venue_profiles.cover_image_url) are fixed by 20260925210000_venue_profile_presentation_columns.sql once an operator applies it; 124 remain and are routed to 23 handoffs.

Regeneration is itself blocked until DB-008 reconciles the out-of-band DDL: the generated contract contains columns the active chain does not create (public.venue_profiles has 42 declared columns and 19 created by the chain), so a chain-only regeneration would DELETE real coverage. See knownGaps in the inventory.

QA can close HF-QA-003 once the typecheck delta is measured. The E2E job budget and the 15 skipped release-gate steps stay blocked until then, because typescript.ignoreBuildErrors is still false in next.config.ts.
